propositions: Store-wide compaction spawns one git log --full-history child per ticket inside the global write lock, holding it for minutes and stalling all writers in the fleet
The per-ticket history walk performs N full-history scans (one per ticket) with a leading-wildcard pathspec that defeats pathspec pruning, degrading the real cost below one-per-ticket
The sweep never re-yields mid-run: it probes write_lock_is_busy once before starting and never again during the per-ticket loop, blocking writers that arrive after sweep start
The staging in _commit_backfill uses unscoped git add -A, allowing concurrent writer in-flight event files to be committed under the compactor message instead of remaining live

Hoisting the position-keyed map build (_sweep_position_map) out of the lock and reusing it per ticket reduces the critical section to SNAPSHOT write, renames and commit only, removing all git log cost from the write lock hold
